Build Prompt: odk-central-operators — Production-Grade Juju K8s Charm Group

This document is a self-contained build prompt for a dev-box agent session. The consuming agent may not be Claude Code. It runs unattended (equivalent to --dangerously-skip-permissions) on a machine with juju, charmcraft, git, and a bootstrapped Kubernetes. Prefer Canonical Kubernetes (k8s) wherever the choice arises; microk8s is a fallback only. No interactive checkpoints occur after Phase 0.

References to mastodon-operator, sentry-operators, hedgedoc-operator, windmill-operators, zammad-operator, flagsmith-operators, tracecat-operator and dependencytrack-operators in the tonyandrewmeyer/ namespace on GitHub are prior operator work used here as background context on repository conventions only. This charm group is not derived from them.

What is being built. ODK Central is the server half of the ODK ecosystem: forms authored as XLSForm spreadsheets are converted to XForms, filled in offline on a mobile client or in a browser, and submitted back to Central. Upstream ships it as an eight-container Docker Compose stack. This build produces three charms in one repository, deployed as a group, plus the two charm libraries that bind them together.

Desk recon and scoring for this candidate: RECON-odk-central.md in non-roadmap/own-a-charm/ of the work-queue repo. Category context: RECON-forms.md. Read neither to build — everything needed is below.

USER ANSWERS REQUIRED — Read Before Phase 0

Collect all answers before running Phase 0. The build does not pause again after Phase 0 completes.

Q1 — GitHub namespace
     Which GitHub user or organisation hosts the repo?
     Default: tonyandrewmeyer
     The repository will be created at <namespace>/odk-central-operators.
     It holds all three charms; there is no separate repo per charm.

Q2 — Juju k8s controller name
     What is the name of the bootstrapped Kubernetes controller?
     Run to list available: juju controllers --format=yaml
     Canonical Kubernetes (k8s) is preferred over microk8s. If both are
     bootstrapped, use the k8s one.

Q3 — ODK Central version to target
     Which release should the charms pin on day one?
     To find the latest, list the tags on the official image:
       TOKEN=$(curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:getodk/central-service:pull&service=ghcr.io" | jq -r .token)
       curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
         https://ghcr.io/v2/getodk/central-service/tags/list | jq -r '.tags[-5:]'
     Recommended starting point as of 2026-08-25: v2026.2.4
     Write the tag with the leading "v": v2026.2.4
     The same tag pins BOTH central-service and central-nginx — they are
     released together and must not be mismatched.

Q4 — Enketo and pyxform versions
     Enketo default: 7.6.1  (ghcr.io/enketo/enketo)
     pyxform default: v4.5.0 (ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http)
     These are pinned independently of Q3. Confirm the versions the
     chosen Central release expects by reading enketo.dockerfile and
     docker-compose.yml at the Q3 tag of getodk/central:
       https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getodk/central/<Q3>/enketo.dockerfile
       https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getodk/central/<Q3>/docker-compose.yml
     If those files name different versions, the upstream files win.

Q5 — Redis backing for Enketo
     Enketo needs two Redis instances with different persistence
     semantics. Charmhub has no stable Redis charm (redis-k8s is
     latest/edge revision 23, released 2022-12-05).
     Default: in-charm — run both as sidecar containers inside
     enketo-k8s, with Juju filesystem storage for the durable one.
     Alternative: relate — wire optional redis-main / redis-cache
     relations and deploy redis-k8s from latest/edge.
     Default: in-charm (the relations are still declared and take
     precedence when present; see Architecture Decisions).
     Answer: in-charm or relate

Q6 — Public domain name
     The fully qualified domain the deployment will be reached at.
     ODK Central will not work with a bare IP address — the frontend
     bakes the origin into its client config and Enketo's linked-server
     URL must match.
     For a test deploy, a nip.io style name against the traefik
     external IP is acceptable, e.g. odk.10-0-0-5.nip.io
     Example: odk.example.com

Q7 — Initial admin email
     Email address for the first Central web user, which the
     create-admin action promotes to administrator.
     Stored as a Juju secret, never in charm config.
     Example: ops-team@example.com

Q8 — Day-one authentication mode
     Options: password, oidc
     Default: password
     IMPORTANT: these are mutually exclusive upstream. With OIDC
     enabled, HTTP Basic auth and POST /v1/session stop working
     entirely. This answer controls what Phase 4's smoke test and the
     Phase 10 integration suite authenticate with. OIDC is wired and
     tested in Phase 8 regardless of this answer.

Q9 — Charmhub entity names and track
     Defaults: odk-central-k8s, enketo-k8s, pyxform-k8s
     Default track: latest
     Central uses date-based versions (2026.2.x), so a version track
     would need renaming every quarter; latest/edge → latest/candidate
     is the intended promotion path. Confirm or supply alternatives.

Q10 — Error reporting
     Upstream's shipped compose defaults contain ODK's OWN Sentry DSN,
     organisation subdomain and project key. A naive deploy reports
     errors to the ODK project's telemetry.
     Default: disabled — the charm blanks every SENTRY_* value unless
     an operator sets its own DSN via config.
     Answer: disabled, or supply your own DSN.

Architecture Decisions (pre-resolved)

These decisions are final. Do not re-debate them during the build.

Kubernetes-only for v1. postgresql-k8s, traefik-k8s, s3-integrator, smtp-integrator and the COS charms all have mature k8s variants, and upstream ships only container images. A machine charm is out of scope for this build.

Three Juju applications, seven containers. The group is:

Charm Containers Why separate
odk-central-k8s service, nginx The API and the frontend/reverse-proxy are released together and version-locked; they belong in one application
enketo-k8s enketo, plus redis-main and redis-cache under Q5 default Enketo is an independently versioned upstream (enketo/enketo) with its own state; it scales and upgrades on its own cadence
pyxform-k8s pyxform A stateless XLSForm→XForm converter with its own release train; separating it makes the conversion service replaceable and independently scalable

Do not collapse these into one application. The cross-charm bootstrap ordering and the provided interface are the point of the exercise.

SSL_TYPE=upstream. Upstream's nginx image can obtain Let's Encrypt certificates itself. In Juju, TLS is traefik-k8s's job. Set SSL_TYPE=upstream so nginx serves plain HTTP on 80 and trusts X-Forwarded-Proto. Never enable certbot inside the charm.

No secrets container. Upstream's one-shot secrets container writes three files to a shared Docker volume. Juju has no shared volume between applications, so odk-central-k8s generates all three values in its install hook, stores them as application-owned Juju secrets, and distributes them to enketo-k8s over the odk-enketo relation. This is the charm-group design's centrepiece.

Exact secret lengths are load-bearing. files/enketo/start-enketo.sh upstream asserts, with stat -c "%s", that /etc/secrets/enketo-secret is exactly 64 bytes, /etc/secrets/enketo-less-secret exactly 32 bytes, and /etc/secrets/enketo-api-key exactly 128 bytes. Enketo refuses to start otherwise. When the enketo-k8s charm pushes these files with Pebble, write no trailing newline and assert the length in charm code before pushing. A stray \n is a 65-byte file and a hard startup failure with an unhelpful message.

Two new charm libraries, written here. No published charmlib exists for either interface. Write and ship:

  • lib/charms/odk_central_k8s/v0/odk_enketo.py — OdkEnketoProvider (in odk-central-k8s) and OdkEnketoRequirer (in enketo-k8s). Provider sends: secret IDs for the three shared secrets, and the public base URL. Requirer sends back: the in-cluster Enketo URL that Central puts in config.json under enketo.url.
  • lib/charms/pyxform_k8s/v0/xlsform.py — XlsformProvider (in pyxform-k8s) and XlsformRequirer (in odk-central-k8s). Provider sends host and port; requirer consumes them into config.json under xlsform.

Both are bidirectional; model them on data_platform_libs conventions for event naming (*_ready, *_gone) and emit custom events rather than making the charm handle raw relation-changed.

Charm libraries over hand-rolled requirers everywhere else. Where a published charmlib exists for a relation interface, import it. Hand rolling is acceptable only for the two ODK-specific interfaces above.

Redis default is in-charm (Q5). redis-main and redis-cache run as sidecar containers in enketo-k8s, redis-main mounting a Juju filesystem storage at /data with upstream's persistence settings (save 300 1, appendonly no, dbfilename enketo-main.rdb) and redis-cache running with persistence off. The charm ALSO declares optional redis-main and redis-cache relations (interface redis); when either is related, the corresponding sidecar is stopped and the relation endpoint is used instead. Attempt the relation path once in Phase 6 against redis-k8s --channel latest/edge and record the result in docs/day2-ops.md whichever way it goes.

jubilant for integration tests, ops.testing for unit tests. Do not use pytest-operator.

Juju secrets for every credential. No password, key, token or DSN appears in config:.

charmcraft 4.x + ops 3.x. Verify at Phase 0; if newer minors are available, use them. Do not pin below these majors.

Apache 2.0 for the charms. The upstream workload is Apache-2.0 throughout — getodk/central, central-backend, central-frontend and enketo/enketo — so unlike most candidates in this category there is no licence divergence to document. Say so explicitly in CONTRIBUTING.md; it is the reason this upstream was chosen.

mkdocs-material for the docs site, one site for all three charms.

release-please for release automation, uv for Python dependency management, Conventional Commits throughout.

Commit directly to origin/main. No feature branches. Each phase ends with a commit and git push -u origin main.

Pebble service startup order

odk-central-k8s:

  1. Block until postgresql relation data is complete.
  2. Render /usr/odk/config/local.json (or wherever the image expects its config — verify against the image, see Phase 4) from the template, including database, email, xlsform, enketo, oidc and s3blobStore stanzas.
  3. Run migrations as a one-shot Pebble service (migrations, startup: disabled, started by charm code, exit code checked).
  4. Start service; gate ActiveStatus on GET http://localhost:8383/v1/version.json returning 200.
  5. Start nginx only once service is healthy — the nginx config proxies to it and will fail its own healthcheck otherwise.

nginx additionally needs DOMAIN, SSL_TYPE=upstream, HTTPS_PORT and OIDC_ENABLED in its environment because it templates client-config.json for the browser at container start. Changing any of those is a re-render and reload, not just a restart: the file is read by the frontend at page load.

enketo-k8s:

  1. Start redis-main and redis-cache (or verify the relations).
  2. Block until the odk-enketo relation supplies all three secrets and the base URL.
  3. Push /etc/secrets/enketo-secret (64 B), enketo-less-secret (32 B), enketo-api-key (128 B) with exact lengths, no newline.
  4. Render config.json from the template with SECRET, LESS_SECRET, API_KEY, BASE_URL, DOMAIN and the two Redis endpoints.
  5. Start enketo; gate ActiveStatus on port 8005 accepting connections.

pyxform-k8s: single service, starts immediately, no dependencies. It is the only charm in the group that can reach ActiveStatus standalone.

Cross-charm bootstrap ordering

pyxform-k8s ──(xlsform)──▶ odk-central-k8s ──(odk-enketo)──▶ enketo-k8s
                                  ▲                                │
                                  └──── enketo URL sent back ──────┘

odk-central-k8s cannot render a complete config.json until BOTH the xlsform relation (host/port) and the odk-enketo relation (Enketo's URL, which Enketo only sends after it has received the secrets Central generated) are settled. That is a genuine two-way bootstrap: Central must publish secrets before Enketo can start, and Enketo must publish its URL before Central's config is complete.

Implement it as: Central writes secrets and base URL immediately on relation-created; Central starts with enketo.url pointing at a placeholder and sets WaitingStatus("waiting for enketo"); on receiving Enketo's URL it re-renders and restarts service. Do not block Central's startup on Enketo — that deadlocks the group.

External ports (charm-internal; traefik maps these)

  • service: 8383 (HTTP, API)
  • nginx: 80 (HTTP, serves frontend + proxies /v1 to service and /- to Enketo)
  • enketo: 8005 (HTTP)
  • pyxform: 80 (HTTP)
  • redis-main: 6379, redis-cache: 6380 (note the non-default port on the cache instance — upstream's config sets it and Enketo's config expects it)

Storage requirements

  • odk-central-k8s: none. All state is in PostgreSQL and, once the S3 relation exists, the blob store.
  • enketo-k8s: redis-main-data, type: filesystem, minimum-size: 1G, mounted at /data in the redis-main container. redis-cache is deliberately ephemeral.
  • pyxform-k8s: none.

Losing redis-main loses in-flight form and instance state in Enketo. Say so in docs/day2-ops.md — it is the one piece of state in the group that is not in PostgreSQL or S3.

Configuration & Secret Surface

odk-central-k8s config

Key Type Default Description
external-hostname string "" Public FQDN (Q6). Overrides the ingress-supplied hostname when set. Central will not work with a bare IP
sysadmin-email string "" Address shown to users as the system contact; also used as the Let's Encrypt contact upstream, unused here
email-from string "" Envelope From for outbound mail. Defaults to no-reply@<external-hostname> when empty
session-lifetime int 86400 Web session lifetime in seconds
db-pool-size int 10 Per-worker PostgreSQL connection pool size
log-level string INFO Workload log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR
oidc-enabled bool false Enable OpenID Connect. Disables password auth and POST /v1/session entirely — see Phase 8
oidc-issuer-url string "" OIDC issuer URL. Ignored when the oauth relation is present, which supplies it
oidc-client-id string "" OIDC client ID (public, non-sensitive). Ignored when the oauth relation is present
s3-bucket-name string "" Override the bucket name supplied by the s3 relation
s3-upload-interval-minutes int 15 How often the charm triggers the pending-blob upload job
error-reporting-dsn string "" Operator's own Sentry DSN. Empty means all SENTRY_* values are blanked — upstream's shipped defaults are ODK's own project and must never be inherited (Q10)

Key Type Default Description

Key Type Default Description

Secret surface (Juju secrets — never config:)

Secrets with no operator-supplied value are generated by odk-central-k8s on first install. Operator-supplied ones are marked OPERATOR-PROVIDED.

Juju secret label Contents Source Notes
odk-enketo-api-key Exactly 128 characters Generated Shared with Enketo over the relation; also written into Central's own enketo.apiKey
odk-enketo-secret Exactly 64 characters Generated Enketo's encryption key
odk-enketo-less-secret Exactly 32 characters Generated Enketo's "less secure" encryption key
odk-admin-email Email string OPERATOR-PROVIDED (Q7) Consumed by the create-admin action
odk-admin-password Password string Generated if absent Returned once by create-admin; never logged
odk-oidc-client-secret OIDC client secret OPERATOR-PROVIDED Only when oidc-enabled=true and no oauth relation
— S3 access/secret key s3 relation Never a Juju secret owned by this charm
— SMTP user/password smtp relation Never a Juju secret owned by this charm

Generate with secrets.token_urlsafe() trimmed (or secrets.choice over an explicit alphabet) to the exact lengths above, then assert len(value) == N before storing. Store via self.app.add_secret({...}, label=...); on later hooks retrieve rather than regenerate.

SECRET_ID=$(juju secret add odk-admin-email email=<Q7-value> --format json | jq -r .secret-id)
juju grant-secret $SECRET_ID odk-central-k8s
juju config odk-central-k8s admin-email-secret=$SECRET_ID

Relation and config → config.json mapping

Central reads a JSON config file, not environment variables. The charm renders it; upstream's files/service/config.json.template is the authoritative shape.

config.json path Source
database.host / .user / .password / .database postgresql relation
database.maximumPoolSize db-pool-size config
email.serviceAccount email-from config
email.transportOpts.host / .port / .secure / .auth.* smtp relation
sessionLifetime session-lifetime config
xlsform.host / .port xlsform relation (pyxform-k8s)
enketo.url odk-enketo relation (Enketo's in-cluster URL + /-)
enketo.apiKey Juju secret odk-enketo-api-key
env.domain ingress URL or external-hostname config
env.sysadminAccount sysadmin-email config
oidc.enabled oidc-enabled config
oidc.issuerUrl / .clientId oauth relation, else config
oidc.clientSecret oauth relation, else Juju secret
external.sentry.* error-reporting-dsn config; blank by default
external.s3blobStore.server / .accessKey / .secretKey / .bucketName s3 relation, bucket overridable by config

nginx container environment

Env var Source
DOMAIN ingress URL host or external-hostname
SSL_TYPE hardcoded upstream
HTTPS_PORT hardcoded 443

SENTRY_* / SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND blanked unless error-reporting-dsn set

Phase 0 — Pre-flight & Answers

Goals: Verify the dev box is ready; print a build manifest; block on any missing prerequisite before writing a line of charm code.

Steps:

  1. Verify tool versions: bash juju version # must be >= 3.6 charmcraft version # must be >= 4.0 git --version python3 --version # must be >= 3.12 uv --version # install: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

  2. Verify the k8s controller (Q2) and prefer Canonical Kubernetes: bash juju controllers --format=yaml juju switch <Q2-controller> juju status --format=yaml | head -5

  3. Verify the GitHub repository exists or can be created at <Q1>/odk-central-operators. If it does not exist, create it empty.

  4. Confirm every image tag resolves before pinning it: bash for img in "getodk/central-service:<Q3>" "getodk/central-nginx:<Q3>" \ "getodk/pyxform-http:<Q4-pyxform>" "enketo/enketo:<Q4-enketo>"; do repo="${img%:*}"; tag="${img##*:}" tok=$(curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:$repo:pull&service=ghcr.io" | jq -r .token) code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $tok" \ "https://ghcr.io/v2/$repo/manifests/$tag" \ -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json") echo "$img -> $code" # 200 required done

  5. Download the upstream reference files for the Q3 tag into hack/upstream/ and keep them in the repo as the source of truth for later phases: bash mkdir -p hack/upstream base=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getodk/central/<Q3> for f in docker-compose.yml .env.template enketo.dockerfile \ files/service/config.json.template \ files/enketo/config.json.template \ files/enketo/start-enketo.sh \ files/enketo/redis-enketo-main.conf \ files/enketo/redis-enketo-cache.conf \ files/nginx/odk.conf.template \ files/nginx/client-config.json.template; do curl -sfSL "$base/$f" -o "hack/upstream/$(basename $f)" || echo "MISSING: $f" done If any file is missing at that tag, the upstream layout has changed — re-derive the component map from what is actually there before continuing. Upstream files always win over this document.

  6. Print a one-page build manifest summarising Q1–Q10 and the installed tool versions. Proceed immediately if unattended.

Commit: none — Phase 0 is pre-work only.

Phase 1 — Repository Scaffold

Goals: A well-structured multi-charm open-source repository with all OSS hygiene files in place; CI green on the empty scaffold.

Layout:

odk-central-operators/
  charms/
    odk-central-k8s/
    enketo-k8s/
    pyxform-k8s/
  lib/                     # shared: the two ODK charm libraries live
                           # in each charm's own lib/ (symlinked from here)
  hack/upstream/           # Phase 0 reference files
  docs/
  tests/integration/       # group-level tests, not per-charm
  .github/
  mkdocs.yml
  pyproject.toml           # workspace root; each charm has its own too

Steps:

  1. Clone (or init) <Q1>/odk-central-operators and work on main.

  2. Create root files:

LICENSE — Apache 2.0 from https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt, with Copyright 2026 Canonical Ltd.

README.md — structure: ``` # odk-central-operators

Juju charms for ODK Central, an open-source platform for collecting, managing and using survey and field data.

## What is ODK Central? [two sentences from the upstream docs]

## The charm group [table: odk-central-k8s / enketo-k8s / pyxform-k8s, what each runs]

## Quick start [juju deploy commands, 15 lines max]

## Relation matrix [table of all relations across all three charms]

## Day-2 operations [table of all actions with brief descriptions]

## Observability [COS-Lite wiring paragraph]

## Contributing See CONTRIBUTING.md. ```

CONTRIBUTING.md — uv dev setup, per-charm unit tests (uv run pytest charms/<name>/tests/unit), group integration tests (uv run pytest tests/integration), pre-commit, Conventional Commits. State explicitly that both the charms and the upstream workload are Apache-2.0 — unusually for this software category there is no licence divergence and no enterprise-gated code in the deployed images.

CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md — Contributor Covenant 2.1.

SECURITY.md — report via security@ubuntu.com, response within 5 business days, coordinated disclosure; reference https://ubuntu.com/security/disclosure-policy. Add a line pointing upstream reports at https://github.com/getodk/central/security.

CHANGELOG.md — Keep-a-Changelog, seeded with ## [Unreleased].

  1. Create .github/:

  2. ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md — fields: which charm, ODK Central version, charm revision, Juju version, k8s flavour, reproduction, expected vs actual.

  3. ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md.
  4. PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md — tests added, CHANGELOG updated, conventional commit, juju status attached if integration-relevant.

    jobs: lint: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5 - run: uv run pre-commit run --all-files

    unit-tests: runs-on: ubuntu-latest strategy: matrix: charm: [odk-central-k8s, enketo-k8s, pyxform-k8s] steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5 - run: uv run pytest charms/${{ matrix.charm }}/tests/unit -v

    integration-tests: if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: canonical/setup-lxd@v0 - uses: charmed-kubernetes/actions-operator@main with: provider: microk8s channel: 1.32-strict/stable - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5 - run: uv run pytest tests/integration -v `` (CI runners use microk8s because Canonical Kubernetes is not yet a packaged GitHub Actions provider; the dev-box build still usesk8sper Q2. Note the discrepancy inCONTRIBUTING.md.) -workflows/release.yml—release-please,release-type: simple. -workflows/security.yml—zizmoron the workflows, weekly cron, plusdependency-reviewon PRs. -workflows/docs.yml—mkdocs gh-deploy --forceon push to main. -dependabot.yml—pipandgithub-actions, weekly, with adirectory` entry per charm.

Docs skeleton and mkdocs.yml: docs/ index.md — what the group is, and why three charms quickstart.md — deploy to first submission architecture.md — the component map and bootstrap ordering configuration.md — every config key of all three charms relations.md — what to deploy and integrate, and why day2-ops.md — backup, restore, upgrade, secret rotation observability.md — COS-Lite wiring and shipped dashboards migrating-from-compose.md — moving an existing compose deploy contributing.md

Apache 2.0 licence, contributing guides, code of conduct, security policy, GitHub Actions CI matrix over three charms, release-please, zizmor, dependabot, pre-commit with ruff+mypy+yamllint+actionlint, mkdocs-material docs skeleton, uv workspace." git push -u origin main ```

Phase 2 — Charm Scaffolding

Goals: Three compilable, packable charms with correct charmcraft.yaml files. No relations wired; no workload started. charmcraft pack produces three .charm files.

Steps:

  1. For each charm, run charmcraft init --profile kubernetes --name <entity> in a scratch directory and merge the result into charms/<entity>/. Discard the generated README.md.

  2. Write each charmcraft.yaml in full — name, type: charm, title, summary, description, links (documentation, issues, source, website https://docs.getodk.org), bases (ubuntu 24.04 build-on/run-on), containers, resources, storage, the relation matrix from the Relation Surface section, the full config: block from the Configuration & Secret Surface section, and the actions: block below.

odk-central-k8s resources: yaml resources: service-image: type: oci-image description: ODK Central API service upstream-source: ghcr.io/getodk/central-service:<Q3> nginx-image: type: oci-image description: ODK Central nginx + built frontend upstream-source: ghcr.io/getodk/central-nginx:<Q3>

enketo-k8s resources: enketo-image (ghcr.io/enketo/enketo:<Q4>) and redis-image (redis:8.6.4, used by both Redis containers).

pyxform-k8s resources: pyxform-image (ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http:<Q4>).

odk-central-k8s actions: yaml actions: create-admin: description: | Create the initial web user from the odk-admin-email Juju secret and promote it to administrator. Returns the generated password once; it is not retrievable afterwards. promote-user: description: Grant an existing user the administrator role. params: email: {type: string, description: Address of the user to promote.} reset-password: description: Reset a user's password and return the new value once. params: email: {type: string, description: Address of the user.} rotate-enketo-secrets: description: | Regenerate all three Enketo shared secrets, republish them over the odk-enketo relation, and restart both workloads. All in-progress web form sessions are invalidated. run-migrations: description: Run database migrations manually (normally automatic on refresh). upload-pending-blobs: description: | Upload submission attachments still held in PostgreSQL to the S3 blob store. No-op without an s3 relation. purge-deleted: description: Permanently remove soft-deleted forms and submissions. params: force: {type: boolean, default: false, description: Skip the retention window.} backup: description: pg_dump the Central database to the S3 blob store. params: destination: {type: string, description: S3 path prefix for the backup output.} restore: description: Restore the Central database from a backup snapshot. params: source: {type: string, description: S3 path prefix of the backup.}

enketo-k8s actions: flush-cache (flush the cache Redis instance only, never the durable one) and redis-info (return INFO output from both instances for diagnosis).

pyxform-k8s actions: convert (accept an XLSForm as a base64 param and return the XForm — a diagnostic, not a production path).

  1. Run charmcraft fetch-lib for every library in the Relation Surface section, in each charm that needs it. Commit the lib/ trees.

  2. Write the two ODK charm libraries as skeletons with full docstrings, LIBID/LIBAPI/LIBPATCH, provider and requirer classes, and custom events — but with pass bodies for the data handling, which Phases 5 and 6 fill in. Getting the API shape fixed now stops the two charms drifting apart later.

  3. Write a minimal src/charm.py per charm that imports ops, defines the charm class, handles install, config-changed and upgrade-charm as stubs, and sets ops.WaitingStatus("waiting for relations") on startup.

  4. Pack all three: bash for c in odk-central-k8s enketo-k8s pyxform-k8s; do (cd charms/$c && charmcraft pack) done ls -la charms/*/*.charm

  5. Commit: ```bash git commit -m "feat(charms): charmcraft scaffolds for all three charms

charmcraft.yaml for odk-central-k8s, enketo-k8s and pyxform-k8s with full container, resource, storage, relation, config and action surfaces. Fetched charm libs. Skeletons for the odk_enketo and xlsform libraries. charmcraft pack produces three valid artefacts." git push -u origin main ```

Definition of done: three .charm files exist; every uv run pytest charms/*/tests/unit leg passes.

Phase 3 — pyxform-k8s End to End

Goals: The simplest charm in the group, complete: workload running, xlsform interface implemented and published, unit tests, deployed and active/idle. Doing this charm first fixes the library conventions the other two follow.

Steps:

  1. Implement the Pebble layer for the pyxform container. Verify the image's entrypoint first: bash docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http:<Q4> >/dev/null docker create --name tmp-pyxform ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http:<Q4> docker inspect tmp-pyxform --format='{{json .Config.Entrypoint}} {{json .Config.Cmd}}' docker rm tmp-pyxform The upstream compose runs the image with no command override, so the Pebble command is the image's own entrypoint plus whatever worker/timeout flags workers and conversion-timeout config map to. If the image exposes no such flags, apply them as environment variables and record what you found in docs/configuration.md.

  2. Implement XlsformProvider in lib/charms/pyxform_k8s/v0/xlsform.py: on relation-joined and on any change to the service's bound address, write host and port into the application relation databag; emit XlsformReadyEvent on the requirer side.

  3. Gate ActiveStatus on a real conversion, not a port check: POST a two-row minimal XLSForm to the service and assert a valid XForm comes back. Keep that fixture in charms/pyxform-k8s/tests/data/minimal.xlsx.

  4. Unit tests: service starts on pebble-ready; relation databag populated on join; status blocked when the conversion probe fails.

  5. Smoke test: bash juju add-model odk-test juju deploy ./charms/pyxform-k8s/pyxform-k8s_amd64.charm \ --resource pyxform-image=ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http:<Q4> juju wait-for application pyxform-k8s --query='status=="active"' --timeout=10m

  6. Commit: feat(pyxform): workload, xlsform interface, conversion probe.

Definition of done: pyxform-k8s reaches active/idle standalone; the conversion probe passes; unit tests green.

Phase 4 — odk-central-k8s Single-Container Baseline

Goals: The Central API service runs under Pebble against a PostgreSQL relation; migrations run before the service starts; the charm reports active/idle; /v1/version.json answers.

Phase 4 deliberately excludes nginx, Enketo, S3, SMTP and OIDC. Render config.json with the xlsform stanza from the Phase 3 relation, an enketo.url placeholder, empty s3blobStore, blanked sentry, and a null email transport. Central starts without a working mail transport; it only fails when something tries to send.

Steps:

  1. Determine where the image expects its config and how it starts: bash docker create --name tmp-svc ghcr.io/getodk/central-service:<Q3> docker inspect tmp-svc --format='{{json .Config.Entrypoint}} {{json .Config.Cmd}} {{json .Config.WorkingDir}}' docker export tmp-svc | tar -t | grep -E 'start-odk|config/(local|default)\.json' | head docker rm tmp-svc hack/upstream/config.json.template gives the required shape; the image's own start-odk.sh gives the path and the render step. The image's files are authoritative — this document is not.

  2. Implement _render_service_config() returning the full config.json dict from the mapping table above, and push it with container.push(path, json.dumps(cfg, indent=2), make_dirs=True).

  3. Pebble layer for the service container: python ops.pebble.Layer({ "summary": "odk central service", "services": { "migrations": { "override": "replace", "summary": "database migrations (one-shot)", "command": "<verified migration command>", "startup": "disabled", "environment": self._service_env(), }, "service": { "override": "replace", "summary": "ODK Central API", "command": "<verified start command>", "startup": "disabled", "environment": self._service_env(), "on-failure": "restart", }, }, "checks": { "api-up": { "override": "replace", "level": "ready", "period": "15s", "threshold": 3, "http": {"url": "http://localhost:8383/v1/version.json"}, }, }, })

  4. Startup sequence, driven from a single _reconcile() that every hook calls (do not scatter logic across per-relation handlers):

  5. Return early with WaitingStatus if the postgresql relation is incomplete.
  6. Generate the three Enketo secrets if absent (they are needed here even before enketo-k8s exists, because enketo.apiKey is part of Central's own config).
  7. Render and push config.json.
  8. container.start("migrations"); poll until the service exits; non-zero exit → BlockedStatus("database migration failed") and return.
  9. Start service; wait for the api-up check to pass.

  10. ActiveStatus("api ready; awaiting enketo") until the odk-enketo relation is settled.

  11. Unit tests: postgres relation complete → migrations run then service starts; postgres incomplete → Waiting; migration non-zero exit → Blocked; secrets generated once and reused on re-run; secret lengths are exactly 128/64/32.

  12. Smoke test: bash juju deploy ./charms/odk-central-k8s/odk-central-k8s_amd64.charm \ --resource service-image=ghcr.io/getodk/central-service:<Q3> \ --resource nginx-image=ghcr.io/getodk/central-nginx:<Q3> --trust juju deploy postgresql-k8s --channel 16/stable --trust juju integrate odk-central-k8s postgresql-k8s juju integrate odk-central-k8s pyxform-k8s juju wait-for application odk-central-k8s --query='status=="active"' --timeout=15m juju ssh --container service odk-central-k8s/0 \ curl -s http://localhost:8383/v1/version.json

  13. Commit: feat(central): postgresql relation, config render, migrations, api service.

Definition of done: active/idle; /v1/version.json returns the Q3 version; unit tests green.

Phase 5 — nginx, Frontend and Ingress

Goals: The nginx container serves the built frontend and proxies the API; traefik-k8s fronts it; the web UI loads in a browser.

Steps:

  1. Wire IngressPerAppRequirer from charms.traefik_k8s.v2.ingress, requesting port 80 (nginx), not

  2. Central's frontend and API must be same-origin.

  3. nginx Pebble layer with the environment from the nginx table above. Read hack/upstream/odk.conf.template and hack/upstream/client-config.json.template to confirm which variables the image's entrypoint substitutes; supply every one of them, including the ones you are blanking.

  4. Config changes to DOMAIN, OIDC_ENABLED or the Sentry values are a re-render and reload, not a restart. The browser reads client-config.json on page load. Implement _reload_nginx() as a Pebble exec of nginx -s reload after the entrypoint's templating step has been re-run, and unit-test that a DOMAIN change triggers it.

  5. Start ordering: nginx must not start before service passes api-up. Express this in charm code, not in Pebble requires — the two services are in different containers and Pebble dependencies do not cross container boundaries.

  6. Set external-hostname (Q6) and verify: bash juju deploy traefik-k8s --channel latest/stable --trust juju integrate odk-central-k8s traefik-k8s juju config odk-central-k8s external-hostname=<Q6> juju run traefik-k8s/0 show-proxied-endpoints curl -sI https://<Q6>/ # 200, HTML curl -s https://<Q6>/v1/version.json

  7. Unit tests: ingress URL propagates into both env.domain in config.json and DOMAIN in the nginx environment; nginx does not start while service is unhealthy; a hostname change reloads nginx.

  8. Commit: feat(central): nginx container, frontend config, traefik ingress.

Definition of done: the Central web UI loads at https://<Q6>/; /v1/version.json answers through the ingress.

Phase 6 — enketo-k8s, Shared Secrets and the Provided Interface

Goals: The group's centrepiece. odk-central-k8s provides three generated secrets over the odk-enketo relation; enketo-k8s consumes them, runs its two Redis instances, and publishes its URL back; Central re-renders and restarts with a real enketo.url.

Steps:

  1. Complete lib/charms/odk_central_k8s/v0/odk_enketo.py.

Provider (odk-central-k8s), on relation-created and on any change to the secrets or the base URL: python self.model.get_secret(label="odk-enketo-api-key").grant(relation) self.model.get_secret(label="odk-enketo-secret").grant(relation) self.model.get_secret(label="odk-enketo-less-secret").grant(relation) relation.data[self.app].update({ "api-key-secret-id": ..., "encryption-key-secret-id": ..., "less-secure-key-secret-id": ..., "base-url": self._public_base_url(), "support-email": self.config["sysadmin-email"], }) Requirer (enketo-k8s) reads the IDs, calls self.model.get_secret(id=...), and emits OdkEnketoReadyEvent. Requirer writes back enketo-url (http://<bind-address>:8005/-); the provider emits EnketoUrlChangedEvent.

  1. Write the three secret files into the enketo container before starting it: python for path, label, length in ( ("/etc/secrets/enketo-secret", "odk-enketo-secret", 64), ("/etc/secrets/enketo-less-secret", "odk-enketo-less-secret", 32), ("/etc/secrets/enketo-api-key", "odk-enketo-api-key", 128), ): value = secret_content[label] if len(value.encode()) != length: # not len(value) — bytes raise RuntimeError(f"{label} must be exactly {length} bytes") container.push(path, value, make_dirs=True, permissions=0o400) No trailing newline. start-enketo.sh stats the files and aborts on any other size.

  2. Render Enketo's config.json from hack/upstream/config.json.template (the Enketo one) using the mapping table above, and push it to the path start-enketo.sh expects. Set hide powered by and the logo fields as upstream does.

  3. Redis containers (Q5 default in-charm): two Pebble services in two containers using the same redis-image resource, each with its own config file pushed by the charm from hack/upstream/redis-enketo-main.conf and redis-enketo-cache.conf, with maxmemory overridden from charm config. redis-main mounts the redis-main-data storage at /data. Keep the cache on port 6380 — Enketo's config expects it and changing it silently breaks nothing until cache lookups start failing.

  4. Optional relation override: if a redis-main or redis-cache relation is present, stop the corresponding sidecar, point Enketo's config at the relation endpoint, and set a status message naming which instances are relation-backed.

  5. Attempt the relation path once, whatever Q5 said: bash juju deploy redis-k8s --channel latest/edge juju integrate enketo-k8s:redis-cache redis-k8s Record what happens — deploys and works, deploys and misbehaves, or fails outright — in docs/day2-ops.md under "Redis backing". This is a genuinely open question (Charmhub has no stable Redis charm; redis-k8s is latest/edge revision 23 from 2022-12-05) and the answer is useful independently of this charm. Then remove the relation and continue with the Q5 choice.

  6. Central side: on EnketoUrlChangedEvent, re-render config.json with the real enketo.url and restart service. Do not restart nginx.

  7. Unit tests, both charms:

  8. secrets granted and IDs published on relation-created;
  9. a 65-byte secret raises before any Pebble push happens;
  10. Enketo blocked while the relation is incomplete;
  11. Central re-renders and restarts on enketo-url arriving;
  12. relation override stops the sidecar and rewrites the config;

  13. rotate-enketo-secrets propagates to Enketo (Phase 7 implements the action; assert the library path here).

  14. End-to-end check — this is the first point the group actually works: bash juju deploy ./charms/enketo-k8s/enketo-k8s_amd64.charm \ --resource enketo-image=ghcr.io/enketo/enketo:<Q4> \ --resource redis-image=redis:8.6.4 juju integrate odk-central-k8s enketo-k8s juju wait-for model odk-test --query='forEach(applications, app => app.status=="active")' --timeout=20m

  15. Commit: feat(enketo): shared-secret provider/requirer, redis pair, enketo workload.

Definition of done: all three charms active/idle; Central's rendered config.json contains Enketo's real in-cluster URL; Enketo started without a secrets-size abort.

Phase 7 — Day-2 Actions

Goals: Every action implemented, tested and documented, including the cross-charm one.

create-admin — read odk-admin-email from the Juju secret; generate a password if odk-admin-password is absent; run Central's admin CLI in the service container via Pebble exec (upstream's odk-cmd — verify the exact invocation with juju ssh --container service odk-central-k8s/0 odk-cmd --help); create the user, then promote it to administrator. Return the password in event.set_results() once, and never log it. If OIDC is enabled, fail with a clear message: the password is meaningless.

promote-user / reset-password — same CLI path, one user argument each. reset-password must fail cleanly under OIDC.

rotate-enketo-secrets — the interesting one: 1. Set MaintenanceStatus("rotating enketo secrets"). 2. Generate three new values at the exact lengths. 3. Update all three Juju secrets (secret.set_content). 4. Republish the IDs over the odk-enketo relation — Enketo's requirer sees secret-changed, rewrites the three files and restarts its workload. 5. Re-render Central's config.json (the API key appears there too) and restart service. 6. Return a warning: all in-progress web form sessions are invalidated and users mid-submission will have to start again. Test that step 4 actually reaches the other charm — a rotation that updates Central and leaves Enketo on the old key produces a 403-on-every-form failure that is very hard to read from the outside.

run-migrations — start the one-shot migrations service, wait, report the exit code and the last 50 log lines.

upload-pending-blobs — no-op with a clear message when there is no s3 relation; otherwise invoke the upstream pending-upload entrypoint via Pebble exec and report how many blobs moved. Also wire this on a timer: a Pebble check is the wrong tool — use an ops update-status-driven trigger honouring s3-upload-interval-minutes, or a Pebble service with a sleep loop if the upstream tooling supports a daemon mode. Say which you chose in docs/day2-ops.md.

purge-deleted — invoke Central's purge path; require force=true to bypass the retention window and say so in the description.

backup — verify the s3 relation; pg_dump --format=custom via Pebble exec against the relation's connection string; upload to <destination>/<timestamp>/central.dump; also record in the results that blobs in S3 are not included and that the bucket needs its own versioning or lifecycle policy. Return the path.

restore — Maintenance status; stop service and nginx; download; pg_restore; run migrations; restart; wait for api-up; Active. Refuse to run if the target database is non-empty unless a force param is passed.

enketo-k8s actions — flush-cache (FLUSHALL against the cache instance only; refuse if pointed at the durable one) and redis-info (return INFO from both).

pyxform-k8s action — convert, taking a base64 XLSForm and returning the XForm, for diagnosis.

Unit tests: one per action covering happy path, missing relation, and Pebble exec failure propagated as a failed action rather than a charm error.

Commit: feat(charms): day-2 actions across the group.

Definition of done: every action runs against the deployed group; create-admin yields a login that works in the UI; rotate-enketo-secrets leaves both workloads consistent.

Phase 8 — S3, SMTP and OIDC

Goals: The three external integrations that turn a working deploy into a production-shaped one.

S3 blob storage

Wire the data-platform S3 library. On relation established, populate external.s3blobStore and re-render. New blobs go to S3; existing blobs stay in PostgreSQL until upload-pending-blobs moves them, so model that partially-migrated state explicitly in the charm's status message (ActiveStatus("N blobs pending upload") when the count is non-zero and the relation exists).

For testing, deploy MinIO as a plain k8s Deployment (hack/minio-test-deploy.yaml, written in this phase) and point s3-integrator at it:

juju deploy s3-integrator --channel latest/stable
juju config s3-integrator endpoint=http://minio.default.svc:9000 \
  bucket=odk-central region=us-east-1 path=/
juju run s3-integrator/0 sync-s3-credentials access-key=... secret-key=...
juju integrate odk-central-k8s s3-integrator

SMTP

Wire charms.smtp_integrator.v0.smtp. Populate email.transportOpts. Central sends on account creation, password reset and project invitation only, so verify with a real action rather than a passive check:

juju deploy smtp-integrator --channel latest/stable
juju config smtp-integrator host=... port=587 auth_type=plain
juju integrate odk-central-k8s smtp-integrator
juju run odk-central-k8s/0 reset-password email=<Q7>

With no SMTP relation, Central must still reach Active — email failure is a per-operation error upstream, not a startup one. Set a status message noting that account email is unavailable.

OIDC

Two paths, both supported:

  • Related: charms.hydra.v0.oauth — request the authorisation code flow with scopes openid profile email and the redirect URI https://<domain>/v1/oidc/callback (verify the exact path against the Q3 release's backend source). Populate oidc.* from the relation.
  • Configured: oidc-enabled, oidc-issuer-url, oidc-client-id config plus the odk-oidc-client-secret Juju secret, for a provider with no charm.

Relation data wins over config when both are present; say so in the status message rather than silently preferring one.

The mode switch is the part to get right. Enabling OIDC disables HTTP Basic and POST /v1/session upstream. So: - oidc-enabled=true must also set OIDC_ENABLED=true in the nginx environment and re-render client-config.json, or the frontend offers a password form that cannot work. - The charm's own health check must stay on the unauthenticated /v1/version.json, never on a session-creating endpoint. - create-admin, promote-user and reset-password must fail with a clear message under OIDC, not with a CLI stack trace. - Toggling oidc-enabled on a running deploy locks out every existing password user. Emit a warning in the status message and document it in docs/day2-ops.md as a one-way door in practice.

Unit tests: relation-over-config precedence; nginx re-render on toggle; password actions blocked under OIDC; health check unaffected.

Commit: feat(central): s3 blob store, smtp, oidc via hydra or config.

Definition of done: a submission attachment lands in the MinIO bucket; reset-password delivers mail; with oidc-enabled=true the UI redirects to the provider and a login round-trips.

Phase 9 — Observability

Goals: COS-Lite first class across all three charms.

Loki. LogProxyConsumer in each charm, forwarding every Pebble service's logs: service, nginx, enketo, redis-main, redis-cache, pyxform. Verify the actual on-disk log paths inside each container rather than assuming /var/log/pebble/<service>/<service>.log.

Prometheus. Check first whether Central exposes metrics:

juju ssh --container service odk-central-k8s/0 curl -s http://localhost:8383/metrics | head

If it does, use MetricsEndpointProvider with a static target on 8383. If it does not, ship an exporter Pebble service in the service container: a small prometheus_client process that authenticates with a dedicated Central app-user token and exposes gauges for project count, form count, submissions in the last hour, and pending-blob count. Do not poll the API more often than every 60 seconds. Redis metrics: run redis_exporter alongside each instance, or parse INFO in the same exporter — either is acceptable, pick one and say which.

Tempo. Wire the tracing charmlib and set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT in the service environment. Check whether central-backend instruments with OpenTelemetry (search the upstream source for opentelemetry); if it does not, do not fake it — wire the relation, note in docs/observability.md that the workload emits no spans today, and leave it there. A tracing relation that silently produces nothing is worse than an honest gap.

Grafana dashboards. src/dashboards/odk-central-overview.json with panels for submissions per hour, API request rate and error rate (from nginx logs via Loki if Prometheus has no HTTP metrics), pending-blob count, Enketo cache hit rate, and pyxform conversion latency. Register with GrafanaDashboardProvider.

Alert rules. src/prometheus_alert_rules/odk-central.rule: - /v1/version.json failing for more than 2 minutes; - pending-blob count rising for more than an hour with an s3 relation present (the upload job has stalled); - redis-main unreachable — this is the one piece of non-PostgreSQL state in the group; - pyxform conversion failure rate above a threshold (a broken converter blocks all form publishing while everything else looks healthy).

Deploy COS-Lite in a second model, offer the endpoints cross-model, and integrate all three charms.

Commit: feat(charms): COS-Lite observability across the group.

Definition of done: the dashboard renders with at least one populated panel; Loki holds logs from all six workload services; alert rules load without error in Prometheus.

Phase 10 — Integration Tests

Goals: A jubilant suite that exercises the whole group, including the paths that only break across charm boundaries.

tests/integration/conftest.py — one module-scoped fixture deploying the full composition from the Relation Surface section into a jubilant.temp_model(), waiting for all applications active, then running create-admin and yielding both the Juju handle and the admin credentials.

tests/integration/test_deploy.py: - test_version_endpoint() — /v1/version.json returns the Q3 version. - test_ui_reachable() — the ingress URL returns 200 and HTML. - test_frontend_config_matches_domain() — fetch client-config.json through the ingress and assert the origin matches external-hostname. This catches the baked-at-build-time frontend problem, which nothing else does.

tests/integration/test_form_lifecycle.py — the end-to-end test that proves all three charms are actually cooperating: 1. Create a project via POST /v1/projects. 2. Upload tests/data/minimal.xlsx as a form (POST /v1/projects/{id}/forms?ignoreWarnings=true) — this exercises pyxform-k8s; a conversion failure surfaces here. 3. Publish the form draft. 4. Fetch the Enketo-backed public link (/v1/projects/{id}/forms/{xml}/public-links or the preview endpoint for the Q3 release) — this exercises enketo-k8s and the shared API key; a secrets mismatch surfaces here as a 403. 5. Submit an instance with an attachment via POST .../submission. 6. Read it back through the OData feed (/v1/projects/{id}/forms/{xml}.svc/Submissions) and assert the value round-trips. 7. With an s3 relation, run upload-pending-blobs and assert the attachment is retrievable through the redirect.

tests/integration/test_secrets.py: - test_rotate_enketo_secrets() — capture a working public form link, run rotate-enketo-secrets, wait for both applications active, and assert the form still renders. A rotation that reaches Central but not Enketo fails here with a 403, which is exactly the regression worth guarding.

tests/integration/test_upgrade.py: - test_refresh_charm() — deploy, refresh all three charms to the freshly packed revision, assert Active regained and the form lifecycle test still passes.

tests/integration/test_day2.py: - test_backup_restore() — backup, drop and recreate the database relation, restore, assert the project and form survive. - test_purge_deleted() — soft-delete a form, purge with force, assert it is gone.

Commit: test(integration): jubilant suite for the full charm group.

Definition of done: the whole suite passes in a clean model; the CI integration job passes on push to main.

Phase 11 — Docs Site

Goals: A complete mkdocs-material site with real values, no placeholders.

docs/index.md — what ODK Central is, and specifically why three charms rather than one. Reproduce the bootstrap-ordering diagram.

docs/quickstart.md — zero to first submission: every juju deploy and juju integrate command, the juju secret add for the admin email, the create-admin action, and how to reach the UI. Include an abbreviated juju status.

docs/architecture.md — the component map, the two ODK-specific interfaces with their databag contents, the secret sizes and why they matter, and the partially-migrated blob state.

docs/configuration.md — every config key of all three charms, auto-generated from the three charmcraft.yaml files by scripts/check-docs.py, with a CI check that fails when the tables and the YAML diverge.

docs/relations.md — per relation: what to deploy, why, the commands, and what the charm's status becomes when it is broken. Include the Redis situation honestly: no stable Redis charm exists on Charmhub, the default is in-charm, and here is what happened when we tried the edge charm in Phase 6.

docs/day2-ops.md — - backup and restore, including that S3 blobs are outside the dump; - what juju refresh does to migrations, and when to run run-migrations by hand; - Enketo secret rotation and its user-visible effect; - the OIDC one-way door; - redis-main is the only non-PostgreSQL, non-S3 state in the group; - disaster-recovery posture: Juju model backup + pg_dump + S3 bucket versioning; - Redis backing notes from Phase 6.

docs/observability.md — COS-Lite wiring, the dashboard, the alert rules table, and the honest note about tracing if the workload does not emit spans.

docs/migrating-from-compose.md — moving an existing upstream Docker Compose deployment: dump and load PostgreSQL, hand the existing Enketo secrets to the charm instead of letting it generate new ones (a juju secret add per value, at the exact lengths), and what to do about the legacy 9.6→14 postgres upgrade container, which has no charm equivalent.

Build and deploy: mkdocs build --strict then mkdocs gh-deploy --force.

Commit: docs: complete mkdocs-material site for the charm group.

Definition of done: mkdocs build --strict exits 0; GitHub Pages serves the site; scripts/check-docs.py passes.

Phase 12 — Release Scaffolding

Goals: First tagged release 0.1.0 with Charmhub upload wiring for all three charms; uploadable but not published to a public channel.

Steps:

  1. Populate CHANGELOG.md [0.1.0] with everything from Phases 1–11.

  2. Tag and push: bash git tag -a 0.1.0 -m "chore(release): 0.1.0 — first production-ready release" git push origin 0.1.0

  3. .github/workflows/charmhub-upload.yml — a matrix over the three charms, upload-only (track commented out): yaml name: Charmhub upload on: push: tags: ['*'] jobs: upload: runs-on: ubuntu-latest strategy: matrix: charm: [odk-central-k8s, enketo-k8s, pyxform-k8s] steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: canonical/charmcraft-actions/upload@v1 with: credentials: ${{ secrets.CHARMHUB_TOKEN }} charm-path: charms/${{ matrix.charm }} charm-name: ${{ matrix.charm }} # track: <Q9-track> # leave commented: upload-only

  4. Register all three names at https://charmhub.io/register-charm (manual; cannot be automated) and add CHARMHUB_TOKEN to the repository secrets.

  5. Verify the upload job produces a revision for each charm (charmcraft status <name>).

  6. Write RELEASE.md describing the manual promotion path, and state the group constraint explicitly: the three charms are released together and odk-central-k8s and its nginx-image are version-locked to the same upstream tag. Promoting one charm alone is how this group breaks.

Final commit:

git commit -m "chore(release): 0.1.0 release scaffolding, Charmhub upload workflow

CHANGELOG 0.1.0 populated. Matrix charmhub-upload workflow across the
three charms (upload-only). RELEASE.md documents the promotion path and
the group version-lock constraint."
git push -u origin main
git push origin 0.1.0

Definition of done: three Charmhub revisions exist; none is in a public channel.

=== enketo.dockerfile ===
FROM ghcr.io/enketo/enketo:7.6.1

ENV ENKETO_SRC_DIR=/srv/src/enketo/packages/enketo-express
WORKDIR ${ENKETO_SRC_DIR}

# we copy the config template twice. eventually we do want to actually template
# it for the sake of the running server, and we can't do this until the container
# is actually running (volumes aren't available on image build). but there are
# also some static values that the client needs to see, and it doesn't in turn
# care about anything the server needs. because the client config is baked at
# build time, we therefore hand it the untemplated config.

COPY files/shared/envsub.awk /scripts/
COPY files/enketo/config.json.template ${ENKETO_SRC_DIR}/config/config.json.template
COPY files/enketo/config.json.template ${ENKETO_SRC_DIR}/config/config.json
COPY files/enketo/start-enketo.sh ${ENKETO_SRC_DIR}/start-enketo.sh

EXPOSE 8005

CMD ["./start-enketo.sh"]

#!/bin/bash -eu
set -o pipefail
shopt -s inherit_errexit

log() { echo >&2 "[$(basename "$0")] $*"; }

assert_size() {
  local f="$1"
  local expectedSize="$2"

  if ! [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
    log "!!! File not found: $f"
    exit 1
  fi

  actualSize="$(stat -c "%s" "$f")"
  if ! [[ "$actualSize" = "$expectedSize" ]]; then
    log "!!!"
    log "!!! Unexpected file size:"
    log "!!!   file: $f"
    log "!!!   expected: $expectedSize b"
    log "!!!   actual:   $actualSize b"
    log "!!!"
    exit 1
  fi
}
if [[ "${ENKETO_SECRETS-}" = "danger-insecure" ]]; then
  log "Skipping secrets check."
else
  log "Checking secrets exist..."
  assert_size /etc/secrets/enketo-secret       64
  assert_size /etc/secrets/enketo-less-secret  32
  assert_size /etc/secrets/enketo-api-key     128
fi

CONFIG_PATH=${ENKETO_SRC_DIR}/config/config.json
log "Generating enketo configuration..."

BASE_URL=$( [ "${HTTPS_PORT}" = 443 ] && echo https://"${DOMAIN}" || echo https://"${DOMAIN}":"${HTTPS_PORT}" ) \
SECRET=$(cat /etc/secrets/enketo-secret) \
LESS_SECRET=$(cat /etc/secrets/enketo-less-secret) \
API_KEY=$(cat /etc/secrets/enketo-api-key) \
/scripts/envsub.awk \
    < "$CONFIG_PATH.template" \
    > "$CONFIG_PATH"

log "Starting enketo..."
exec yarn workspace enketo-express start

===== envsub.awk =====
#!/usr/bin/mawk -f

# Safer implemention of envsubst.
#
# Significant differences:
#
#   * require curly brackets around values
#   * require uppercase
#   * throw error if value is not defined, instead of just using empty string
#
# mawk is the awk implementation common to the containers we need to run this
# script in, so we use it here explicitly.

BEGIN {
  errorCount = 0;
}

{
  while(match($0, /\$\{[A-Z_][A-Z_0-9]*\}/) > 0) {
    k = substr($0, RSTART+2, RLENGTH-3);
    if(k in ENVIRON) {
      v = ENVIRON[k];
    } else {
      print "ERR: var not defined on line " NR ": ${" k "}" > "/dev/stderr";
      ++errorCount;
      v = "!!!VALUE-MISSING: " k "!!!"
    }
    gsub("\$\{" k "\}", v);
  }
  print $0;
}

END {
  if(errorCount > 0) {
    print "" > "/dev/stderr";
    print errorCount " error(s) found." > "/dev/stderr";
    exit 1;
  }
}

===== start-odk.sh =====
#!/bin/bash -eu
set -o pipefail
shopt -s inherit_errexit

# Check for illegal DB_SSL environment variable.
if [[ -v DB_SSL ]] && ! [[ "$DB_SSL" = "null" ]]; then
  echo "!!!"
  echo "!!! You have the DB_SSL variable defined (in your .env file, probably)."
  echo "!!! This variable is no longer supported from Central 2026.1 onwards."
  echo "!!! There is a new way of configuring SSL for your database, please see:"
  echo "!!!"
  echo "!!!   https://docs.getodk.org/central-install-digital-ocean/#using-a-custom-database-server"
  echo "!!!"
  echo "!!! Please refer to the Central 2026.1.0 release notes for more information on this change."
  echo "!!!"
  echo "!!! ODK Central backend will not start until this issue is resolved."
  echo "!!!"
  sleep 60 # reduce resource waste from quick restart and instant failure
  exit 1
fi
unset DB_SSL

# Serialize (as a raw env block) the environment set up by docker, for later
# availability to processes running with a reset environment (such as cronjobs).
# See https://github.com/getodk/central/issues/1747 .
# See `man 5 proc_pid_environ` .
cp --preserve=mode,ownership /proc/self/environ /dev/shm/docker-envblock


echo "generating local service configuration.."

ENKETO_API_KEY=$(cat /etc/secrets/enketo-api-key) \
BASE_URL=$( [ "${HTTPS_PORT}" = 443 ] && echo https://"${DOMAIN}" || echo https://"${DOMAIN}":"${HTTPS_PORT}" ) \
/scripts/envsub.awk \
    < /usr/share/odk/config.json.template \
    > /usr/odk/config/local.json

SENTRY_RELEASE="$(cat sentry-versions/server)"
export SENTRY_RELEASE
# shellcheck disable=SC2089
SENTRY_TAGS="{ \"version.central\": \"$(cat sentry-versions/central)\", \"version.client\": \"$(cat sentry-versions/client)\" }"
# shellcheck disable=SC2090
export SENTRY_TAGS

echo "waiting for PostgreSQL to become connectable to..."
maxTries=15
retries=$((maxTries-1))
while ! pg_isready; do
  if [[ "$retries" = 0 ]]; then
    echo "PostgreSQL not available after $maxTries attempts."
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "PostgreSQL not yet available; sleeping 1 second..."
  sleep 1
  retries=$((retries-1))
done

echo "running migrations.."
node ./lib/bin/run-migrations

# Logs based on SENTRY_RELEASE and SENTRY_TAGS env variables
echo "logging server upgrade.."
node ./lib/bin/log-upgrade

echo "starting cron.."
cron -f &

is_cgroup2() {
  [ -f /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers ]
}

get_memory_limit() {
  local memtot fallback_memtot

  if [ -r /proc/meminfo ]; then
    fallback_memtot=$(awk '/MemTotal/ {print $2 * 1024}' /proc/meminfo)
  else
    fallback_memtot=0
  fi

  if is_cgroup2; then
    if [ -r /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max ]; then
      memtot=$(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max)
    else
      memtot="max"
    fi
    if [ "$memtot" = "max" ]; then
      memtot=$fallback_memtot
    fi
  else
    # cgroup v1
    if [ -r /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes ]; then
      memtot=$(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes)
    else
      memtot=$fallback_memtot
    fi
  fi

  # Force memtot to be an integer (not scientific notation e+09)
  printf "%.0f\n" "$memtot"
}

determine_worker_count() {
  local memtot=$1
  if [ "$memtot" -gt 1100000 ]; then
    echo 4
  else
    echo 1
  fi
}

MEMTOT=$(get_memory_limit)
WORKER_COUNT=$(determine_worker_count "$MEMTOT")
export WORKER_COUNT
echo "using $WORKER_COUNT worker(s) based on available memory ($MEMTOT).."

echo "starting server."
exec npx --no pm2-runtime ./pm2.config.js

===== with-pgenvblock.pl =====
#!/usr/bin/env perl

use warnings;
use strict;


die "Not enough arguments.\nUsage: with-pgenvblock.pl /path/to/envblock program [program-arg, …]\n" if @ARGV < 2;

my $envblockfile = $ARGV[0];

open my $fh, '<:raw', $envblockfile
    or die "Cannot open '" . $envblockfile . "': $!";
my $content = do { local $/; <$fh> };
close $fh;

my @entries = split /\x00/, $content;

for my $entry (@entries) {
    if ($entry =~ /\A(?<varname>PG[^=]+)=(?<varvalue>.*)\Z/m) {
        $ENV{$+{varname}} = $+{varvalue};
    }
}

exec @ARGV[1..$#ARGV]

===== setup-odk.sh (nginx) =====
#!/bin/bash -eu
set -o pipefail
shopt -s inherit_errexit

echo "writing client config..."
if [[ $OIDC_ENABLED != 'true' ]] && [[ $OIDC_ENABLED != 'false' ]]; then
  echo 'OIDC_ENABLED must be either true or false'
  exit 1
fi

/scripts/envsub.awk \
  < /usr/share/odk/nginx/client-config.json.template \
  > /usr/share/nginx/html/client-config.json

# Generate self-signed keys for the incorrect (catch-all) HTTPS listener.  This
# cert should never be seen by legitimate users, so it's not a big deal that
# it's self-signed and won't expire for 1,000 years.
mkdir -p /etc/nginx/ssl
openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:2048 \
    -subj "/CN=invalid.local" \
    -keyout /etc/nginx/ssl/nginx.default.key \
    -out    /etc/nginx/ssl/nginx.default.crt \
    -days 365000

DH_PATH=/etc/dh/nginx.pem
if [ "$SSL_TYPE" != "upstream" ] && [ ! -s "$DH_PATH" ]; then
  openssl dhparam -out "$DH_PATH" 2048
fi

SELFSIGN_PATH="/etc/selfsign/live/$DOMAIN"
if [ "$SSL_TYPE" = "selfsign" ] && [ ! -s "$SELFSIGN_PATH/privkey.pem" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$SELFSIGN_PATH"
  openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 \
    -subj "/C=XX/ST=XXXX/L=XXXX/O=XXXX/CN=localhost" \
    -keyout "$SELFSIGN_PATH/privkey.pem" \
    -out "$SELFSIGN_PATH/fullchain.pem" \
    -days 3650 -nodes -sha256
fi

# start from fresh templates in case ssl type has changed
echo "writing fresh nginx templates..."
# redirector.conf gets deleted if using upstream SSL so copy it back
/scripts/envsub.awk \
  < /usr/share/odk/nginx/redirector.conf \
  > /etc/nginx/conf.d/redirector.conf

CERT_DOMAIN=$( [ "$SSL_TYPE" = "customssl" ] && echo "local" || echo "$DOMAIN") \
SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND_ROOT="$(awk 'sub(/:\/\/[a-z0-9]*@/, "://") && sub(/\/[0-9]+$/, "")' <<<"$SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND")" \
/scripts/envsub.awk \
  < /usr/share/odk/nginx/odk.conf.template \
  > /etc/nginx/conf.d/odk.conf

if [ "$SSL_TYPE" = "letsencrypt" ]; then
  echo "starting nginx for letsencrypt..."
  /bin/bash /scripts/start_nginx_certbot.sh
else
  if [ "$SSL_TYPE" = "upstream" ]; then
    # no need for letsencrypt challenge reply or 80 to 443 redirection
    rm -f /etc/nginx/conf.d/redirector.conf
    # strip out all ssl_* directives
    perl -i -ne 's/listen 443.*/listen 80;/; print if ! /\bssl_/' /etc/nginx/conf.d/odk.conf
    # force https because we expect SSL upstream
    perl -i -pe 's/X-Forwarded-Proto \$scheme/X-Forwarded-Proto https/;' /etc/nginx/conf.d/odk.conf
    echo "starting nginx for upstream ssl..."
  else
    # remove letsencrypt challenge reply, but keep 80 to 443 redirection
    perl -i -ne 'print if $. < 9 || $. > 16' /etc/nginx/conf.d/redirector.conf
    echo "starting nginx for custom ssl and self-signed certs..."
  fi
  exec nginx -g "daemon off;"
fi

# Redis configuration for Enketo's main database instance

#supervised systemd

#daemonize yes

#pidfile /var/run/redis-enketo-cache/redis-server.pid

port 6379

bind 0.0.0.0

timeout 0

tcp-keepalive 0

loglevel notice

#logfile /var/log/redis/redis-enketo-main.log

databases 16

save 300 1

stop-writes-on-bgsave-error yes

rdbcompression yes

rdbchecksum yes

dbfilename enketo-main.rdb

#dir /var/lib/redis/

slave-serve-stale-data yes
slave-read-only yes
repl-disable-tcp-nodelay no
slave-priority 100

appendonly no

lua-time-limit 5000

slowlog-log-slower-than 10000

slowlog-max-len 128

notify-keyspace-events ""

hash-max-ziplist-entries 512
hash-max-ziplist-value 64
list-max-ziplist-entries 512
list-max-ziplist-value 64
set-max-intset-entries 512
zset-max-ziplist-entries 128
zset-max-ziplist-value 64
activerehashing yes
client-output-buffer-limit normal 0 0 0
client-output-buffer-limit slave 256mb 64mb 60
client-output-buffer-limit pubsub 32mb 8mb 60
hz 10
aof-rewrite-incremental-fsync yes

FROM node:24.16.0-slim AS intermediate

ARG FRONTEND_BUILD_MODE
ARG FRONTEND_VERSION

RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates \
        curl \
        git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY ./ ./

RUN files/prebuild/write-version.sh
RUN files/prebuild/build-frontend.sh



# When upgrading:
#
# 1. Use full-length tag, including nginx version.  See:
#    * https://github.com/JonasAlfredsson/docker-nginx-certbot/blob/master/docs/dockerhub_tags.md
#    * https://hub.docker.com/r/jonasal/nginx-certbot/tags
# 2. Look for upstream changes to redirector.conf
# 3. Confirm setup-odk.sh strips out HTTP-01 ACME challenge location.
FROM jonasal/nginx-certbot:6.2.0-nginx1.31.2

EXPOSE 80
EXPOSE 443

# Persist Diffie-Hellman parameters and/or selfsign key
VOLUME [ "/etc/dh", "/etc/selfsign" ]

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y netcat-openbsd

RUN mkdir -p /usr/share/odk/nginx/

COPY files/nginx/setup-odk.sh \
     files/shared/envsub.awk \
     /scripts/

COPY files/nginx/redirector.conf /usr/share/odk/nginx/
COPY files/nginx/common-headers.conf /usr/share/odk/nginx/
COPY files/nginx/robots.txt /usr/share/nginx/html
COPY --from=intermediate dist/ /usr/share/nginx/html
COPY --from=intermediate /tmp/version.txt /usr/share/nginx/html

ENTRYPOINT [ "/scripts/setup-odk.sh" ]

concierge is installing Canonical Kubernetes (k8s 1.32-classic/stable) — good, that's the preferred substrate.

Two landmines found in the nginx template that change the design:

  1. odk.conf.template hardcodes proxy_pass http://enketo:8005 and http://service:8383. service is same-pod (fine as localhost), but enketo is a separate Juju application — that hostname will never resolve. The charm must push its own templates into /usr/share/odk/nginx/ (which is exactly what upstream's compose bind-mount does).
  2. /csp-report proxies to https://${SENTRY_ORG_SUBDOMAIN}.ingest.sentry.io/api/${SENTRY_PROJECT}/.... Naively blanking SENTRY_* per Q10 yields https://.ingest.sentry.io/api//security/ — nginx fails to load that config. Blanking has to remove the block, not just empty the variables.

"""Root pytest configuration for the odk-central-operators workspace."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest


def pytest_sessionfinish(session: pytest.Session, exitstatus: int) -> None:
    """Treat an empty test session as success.

    The CI matrix runs the per-charm unit suites before every charm has tests,
    and ``pytest`` exits 5 ("no tests collected") in that case. An empty suite
    is not a failure for this repository's scaffold phases.
    """
    if exitstatus == pytest.ExitCode.NO_TESTS_COLLECTED:
        session.exitstatus = 0
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# odk-central-operators

Juju charms for [ODK Central](https://getodk.org/), an open-source platform for
collecting, managing and using survey and field data.

[![CI](https://github.com/tonyandrewmeyer/odk-central-operators/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tonyandrewmeyer/odk-central-operators/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

## What is ODK Central?

ODK Central is the server half of the [ODK](https://getodk.org/) ecosystem:
forms authored as XLSForm spreadsheets are converted to XForms, filled in
offline on a mobile client or in a browser, and submitted back to Central. It
manages projects, form versions, submissions, attachments and users, and
exposes everything over a REST and OData API.

## The charm group

Upstream ships ODK Central as an eight-container Docker Compose stack. This
repository deploys it as **three Juju applications** that are designed to be
deployed together.

| Charm | Containers | What it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `odk-central-k8s` | `service`, `nginx` | The Central API (Node/pm2) and the nginx reverse proxy serving the built frontend. Released and version-locked together upstream. |
| `enketo-k8s` | `enketo`, `redis-main`, `redis-cache` | [Enketo](https://github.com/enketo/enketo), which renders XForms as web forms, plus its two Redis instances (durable and cache). |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `pyxform` | The stateless [pyxform](https://github.com/XLSForm/pyxform) HTTP service that converts XLSForm spreadsheets to XForms. |

Upstream's one-shot `secrets` container has no charm equivalent: Juju has no
shared volume between applications, so `odk-central-k8s` generates the three
shared Enketo secrets itself, stores them as application-owned Juju secrets and
distributes them over the `odk-enketo` relation. See
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

## Quick start

```bash
juju add-model odk

juju deploy odk-central-k8s --channel latest/edge --trust
juju deploy enketo-k8s      --channel latest/edge
juju deploy pyxform-k8s     --channel latest/edge

juju deploy postgresql-k8s --channel 16/stable --trust
juju deploy traefik-k8s    --channel latest/stable --trust

juju integrate odk-central-k8s postgresql-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s pyxform-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s enketo-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s traefik-k8s

juju config odk-central-k8s external-hostname=odk.example.com

SECRET_ID=$(juju add-secret odk-admin-email email=ops-team@example.com)
juju grant-secret "$SECRET_ID" odk-central-k8s
juju config odk-central-k8s admin-email-secret="$SECRET_ID"
juju run odk-central-k8s/0 create-admin
```

The full walkthrough, from an empty model to a first submission, is in
[`docs/quickstart.md`](docs/quickstart.md).

## Relation matrix

| Charm | Endpoint | Interface | Role | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `odk-central-k8s` | `odk-enketo` | `odk-enketo` | provides | Ships the three shared secrets and the public base URL to Enketo; receives Enketo's in-cluster URL back |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `postgresql` | `postgresql_client` | requires | Central's application database |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `xlsform` | `odk-xlsform` | requires | pyxform host and port |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `ingress` | `ingress` | requires | Public HTTP ingress via traefik |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `s3` | `s3` | requires | Blob store for submission attachments and form media |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `smtp` | `smtp` | requires | Account creation and password reset email |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `oauth` | `oauth` | requires | OpenID Connect via the Canonical Identity Platform |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `logging` / `metrics-endpoint` / `grafana-dashboard` / `tracing` | COS | requires | Observability |
| `enketo-k8s` | `odk-enketo` | `odk-enketo` | requires | Shared secrets and base URL from Central |
| `enketo-k8s` | `redis-main` / `redis-cache` | `redis` | requires (optional) | External Redis instead of the in-charm sidecars |
| `enketo-k8s` | `logging` / `metrics-endpoint` / `grafana-dashboard` | COS | requires | Observability |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `xlsform` | `odk-xlsform` | provides | Advertises its host and port to Central |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `logging` / `metrics-endpoint` | COS | requires | Observability |

`pyxform-k8s` has no ingress endpoint on purpose: it is reached only by
Central, in-cluster, and must not be exposed.

## Day-2 operations

| Charm | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `odk-central-k8s` | `create-admin` | Create the initial web user from the `odk-admin-email` Juju secret and promote it to administrator. Returns the password once. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `promote-user` | Grant an existing user the administrator role. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `reset-password` | Reset a user's password and return the new value once. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `rotate-enketo-secrets` | Regenerate all three shared Enketo secrets, republish them over the relation and restart both workloads. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `run-migrations` | Run database migrations manually. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `upload-pending-blobs` | Move submission attachments still held in PostgreSQL to the S3 blob store. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `purge-deleted` | Permanently remove soft-deleted forms and submissions. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `backup` | `pg_dump` the Central database to the S3 blob store. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `restore` | Restore the Central database from a backup snapshot. |
| `enketo-k8s` | `flush-cache` | Flush the cache Redis instance only, never the durable one. |
| `enketo-k8s` | `redis-info` | Return `INFO` output from both Redis instances. |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `convert` | Convert a base64-encoded XLSForm and return the XForm. Diagnostic only. |

Full detail, including what each one does to running users, is in
[`docs/day2-ops.md`](docs/day2-ops.md).

## Observability

All three charms are COS-Lite ready. `odk-central-k8s` and `enketo-k8s` forward
every Pebble service's logs to Loki, expose Prometheus metrics, and ship a
Grafana dashboard and alert rules covering API availability, pending blob
uploads, Redis reachability and pyxform conversion failures.

```bash
juju integrate odk-central-k8s grafana-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s prometheus-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s loki-k8s
```

See [`docs/observability.md`](docs/observability.md).

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Licence

Apache 2.0. So is every piece of the workload these charms deploy — see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#licensing).
EOF
