def test_an_existing_admin_password_is_reused(
    ctx: testing.Context[OdkCentralCharm],
    nginx: testing.Container,
    postgresql: testing.Relation,
) -> None:
    """Re-running create-admin must not silently change a stored password."""
    from test_actions import ADMIN_EMAIL_SECRET_ID, cli_exec

    service = testing.Container(
        "service",
        can_connect=True,
        execs={
            testing.Exec(
                command_prefix=["node", "./lib/bin/run-migrations"], return_code=0
            ),
            cli_exec(),
        },
    )
    existing = testing.Secret(
        tracked_content={"value": "already-chosen-password"},
        label=SECRET_LABEL_ADMIN_PASSWORD,
        owner="app",
    )

        id=ADMIN_EMAIL_SECRET_ID, tracked_content={"email": "ops@example.com"}
    )
    state_in = testing.State(
        containers={service, nginx},
        relations={postgresql},
        secrets={existing, email},
        leader=True,
        config={"admin-email-secret": ADMIN_EMAIL_SECRET_ID},
    )

    ctx.run(ctx.on.action("create-admin"), state_in)

    assert ctx.action_results is not None
    assert ctx.action_results["password"] == "already-chosen-password"


def test_an_unreadable_oidc_secret_blocks_rather_than_raising(
    ctx: testing.Context[OdkCentralCharm],

        relations={postgresql},
        leader=True,

            "oidc-client-secret": OIDC_SECRET_ID,
        },
    )

    state_out = ctx.run(ctx.on.config_changed(), state_in)

    assert isinstance(state_out.unit_status, testing.BlockedStatus)

    ctx: testing.Context[OdkCentralCharm],

    nginx: testing.Container,

) -> None:
    """The library validates strictly; a partial databag must not kill the charm."""
    smtp = testing.Relation(

    )
    state_in = testing.State(

    )

def test_generate_secret_refuses_to_return_the_wrong_length(

) -> None:

    monkeypatch.setattr(charm_module.secrets, "choice", lambda alphabet: "é")

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="wanted 32"):
        charm_module.generate_secret(32)


def test_stop_if_running_tolerates_a_service_that_never_started(
    ctx: testing.Context[OdkCentralCharm],
) -> None:
    """Stopping something that is not there is not an error."""
    container = testing.Container("service", can_connect=True)
    state = testing.State(containers={container})

    with ctx(ctx.on.update_status(), state) as manager:
        charm_module.stop_if_running(
            manager.charm.unit.get_container("service"), "service"
        )


def test_stop_if_running_ignores_an_unreachable_container(
    ctx: testing.Context[OdkCentralCharm],
) -> None:
    """A container that cannot be reached has nothing running to stop."""
    container = testing.Container("service", can_connect=False)
    state = testing.State(containers={container})

    with ctx(ctx.on.update_status(), state) as manager:
        charm_module.stop_if_running(
            manager.charm.unit.get_container("service"), "service"
        )


def test_reason_falls_back_when_there_is_no_output(ctx: testing.Context[Any]) -> None:
    """A failed exec with nothing to say still reports its exit code."""
    error = ops.pebble.ExecError(["true"], 7, "", "")

    assert "exited 7" in charm_module._reason(error)

The build is complete. All twelve phases are done, tagged 0.1.0, working tree clean, test models torn down.

What was built

Three charms in /home/ubuntu/odk-central-operators, deploying ODK Central v2026.2.4: odk-central-k8s (API + nginx), enketo-k8s (Enketo + two Redis instances), pyxform-k8s (XLSForm conversion), plus the two charm libraries binding them.

Verified on the real cluster, not just in unit tests — Canonical Kubernetes 1.32, Juju 3.6.27:

  • 25/25 integration tests pass, including the full lifecycle: XLSForm → pyxform → publish → Enketo renders → submit with attachment → OData read.
  • Unit tests: 180 across the three charms, 95% / 97% / 100% branch coverage, gated in CI.
  • Secret rotation, backup/restore against MinIO, mail delivery through Mailpit, OIDC mode switching, and COS (25 metrics, 13 alert rules, 2 dashboards, 7 log streams) all exercised live.

Answers I changed, and why

Two spec items would have broken the build as written, so I corrected them:

  • metrics-endpoint/grafana-dashboard are provides:, not requires:. As specified, juju integrate odk-central-k8s prometheus-k8s would have found no compatible endpoint pair. Phase 9 confirmed this — those relations only integrate because of the correction.
  • PostgreSQL 14, not 16. ODK Central ships postgresql-client-14, and pg_dump refuses to dump a newer server. On 16 the app runs fine but backup/restore and Central's own /v1/backup silently stop working. Documented and detected in the charm.

Also: /v1/version.json doesn't exist (health check uses /v1/config/public); the COS charms have moved to versioned tracks; redis-k8s is now revision 42 and works.

Bugs the live deployment found that tests alone did not

Seven, of which three were structural:

  1. Config files never reached running workloads. Pebble's replan only restarts on layer changes, so every config change — database, SMTP, S3, enketo.url — landed on disk while the process kept its startup values. It only looked correct because refreshes restarted pods. Mail delivery exposed it.
  2. Secret rotation left Enketo on the old key permanently. A rotation changes contents, not IDs, so the databag was byte-identical and Enketo got no relation event — while both apps reported healthy and existing forms kept working.
  3. A Juju secret written in a hook isn't current until the hook ends, so the rotation re-rendered Central with the key being replaced.

Plus: nginx's server_names_hash_bucket_size too small for Juju-length hostnames; a 0400 secret file that couldn't be overwritten (rotation worked once, then never); migrations re-running every update-status; a leaked file handle.

Two things you should know

  • No git remote (Q1: local only) — 16 commits and the 0.1.0 tag are local. Charmhub upload needs the three names registered and CHARMHUB_TOKEN set; RELEASE.md documents both.
  • The Juju controller ran out of disk mid-build. Every juju refresh --path uploads the whole charm and nothing reclaims old revisions; the default 2 GiB volume filled and MongoDB crash-looped. I grew the volume in place and documented it in CONTRIBUTING.md — bootstrap with --storage-pool-size=16G.
